item.title: Spring Boot CI Pipeline Construction with GitHub Actions: Merge Conflicts and Failure Analysis
item.description:
In the software development process, relying solely on local test execution to apply changes risks introducing unstable code into the target branch. Particularly under concurrent development with multiple team members, there is a constant risk that the CI/CD pipeline will fail to trigger correctly due to complex Git branch structures or misconfigurations during conflict resolution.

This article describes how to build an automated build and test verification pipeline for a Spring Boot project using GitHub Actions, as well as the workflow file path displacement issue that occurred during merge conflict resolution and the diagnostic artifact collection mechanism for test failures.

Basic Structure of GitHub Actions and Declarative Pipeline Design

Automated processes (Workflows) executed in GitHub Actions are defined by YAML declaration files placed in a specific directory within the repository. Because the execution engine runs on ephemeral virtual machine containers, dependency setup and execution steps must be explicitly defined without omissions.

Strict Directory Structure Conventions

GitHub Actions pipeline definition files must strictly be placed at the following path:

.github/workflows/ci.yml

If a file is placed outside this path structure (e.g., docs/ci.yml or .github/ci.yml), GitHub’s event detection engine will not recognize it as a workflow definition.

Implementation Example of a Spring Boot CI Workflow

Below is a standard workflow configuration triggered by code pushes to the main branch and pull requests, executing Gradle builds and tests.

name: CI

on:
 push:
 branches: [main]
 pull_request:
 branches: [main]

jobs:
 test:
 runs-on: ubuntu-24.04

 steps:
 - name: Checkout Source Code
 uses: actions/checkout@v4

 - name: Provision Temurin JDK 21
 uses: actions/setup-java@v4
 with:
 distribution: 'temurin'
 java-version: '21'

 - name: Set Executable Permission for Gradle Wrapper
 run: chmod +x ./gradlew

 - name: Execute Automated Unit Tests
 run: ./gradlew test

 - name: Preserve Test Failure Artifacts
 if: failure()
 uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
 with:
 name: test-report
 path: build/reports/tests/test/
 if-no-files-found: warn

Merge Conflicts and Recovery from Workflow Path Displacement

While working on a feature branch (lab/ci), if changes are introduced concurrently on the remote main branch, a merge conflict will occur on the Pull Request.

Conflict Resolution and File Path Inconsistency

Fetch the latest remote status in the local environment and execute the merge.

git switch lab/ci
git fetch cicd
git merge cicd/main

When executing this merge operation (Git 3-way merge ort strategy), the upstream branch’s commit history may unexpectedly cause .github/workflows/ci.yml to be moved (renamed) to docs/ci.yml.

Once the file is moved to the docs/ directory, subsequent push events will no longer trigger GitHub Actions. To resolve this state, Git commands must be used to restore the file placement to the correct directory.

# Move from incorrect path to the standard directory structure
git mv docs/ci.yml .github/workflows/ci.yml

# Commit changes and push to the remote branch
git commit -m "fix: restore workflow definition path"
git push cicd lab/ci

Separation of Structural Mergeability and Application Verification Status

On the Pull Request diagnostic screen, the following two statuses must be clearly distinguished and interpreted:

  1. Git Structural Mergeability (Merge Conflict Status): Indicates whether the commit tree can be merged at the text level. When No conflicts with base branch is displayed, Git’s file merging itself completes successfully.

  2. CI Status Checks (Status Checks): Indicates whether the application build and unit tests succeeded. In the case of All checks have failed, even if it is mergeable at the Git level, the code is in a broken state.

If Branch Protection Rules are not configured, the Merge button remains clickable in the GitHub UI even when tests fail. To make CI function effectively as a quality gate, configuring successful status checks as a mandatory condition for merging is required.

Troubleshooting

1. Workflow does not run and displays “No workflow runs found”

⚠️ Cause: The workflow file placement path is outside .github/workflows/, or there is an indentation syntax error in the YAML file.

🛠️ Solution: Verify whether the file path is under .github/workflows/*.yml. Also verify that the indentation hierarchy (based on 2 spaces) for jobs and steps is correct.

2. Unable to identify detailed causes from console logs on Gradle test failures

⚠️ Cause: Standard output logs from Gradle alone may not fully output details of fragmented assertion failures or configuration file loading errors.

🛠️ Solution: Configure actions/upload-artifact@v4 with the if: failure() condition to save HTML test reports inside build/reports/tests/test/ as artifacts. This allows inspecting detailed stack traces in a browser upon pipeline failures.

3. Push to remote rejected due to secret leak warnings

⚠️ Cause: Files such as .env, hardcoded API keys, or private keys are included in the Git commit history.

🛠️ Solution: Remove the secret information from the codebase and add the target file pattern to .gitignore. If secrets were included in past commit history, immediately revoke and reissue the credentials, and migrate them to a secure store such as GitHub Actions Secrets.

Terminal Log for Verification

Example terminal output during the normalization of pipeline placement and verification of build operations in the local environment.

$ git status
On branch lab/ci
Your branch is up to date with 'cicd/lab/ci'.

nothing to commit, working tree clean

$ ls -la .github/workflows/
total 12
drwxr-xr-x 1 runner 1049000 0 Oct 25 10:15 .
drwxr-xr-x 1 runner 1049000 0 Oct 25 10:15 ..
-rw-r--r-- 1 runner 1049000 824 Oct 25 10:15 ci.yml

$ ./gradlew test
BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 8s
4 actionable tasks: 4 executed

Lessons Learned

💡 1. Non-equivalence of Git Merge Success and Application Health: Even if a merge completes without text conflicts, it does not imply that builds or tests will pass successfully. Automated verification via CI pipelines is indispensable.

💡 2. Compliance with Configuration File Placement Conventions: In automation tools such as GitHub Actions, specific directory structures (.github/workflows/) serve as execution prerequisites; caution is required regarding file movements during branch operations.

💡 3. Retention of Failure Diagnostic Artifacts: To reduce root cause investigation costs during pipeline failures, it is effective to configure the setup to properly save diagnostic files, such as test reports, rather than simply failing with an error.

item.title: Implementation and Verification of Declarative HTTP Clients with Spring Cloud OpenFeign
item.description:
In microservices architectures and external API integrations, directly using standard HTTP clients (such as RestTemplate or lower-level HttpClients) scatters boilerplate code—such as URL string construction, connection pool management, adding request headers, and response deserialization—across the codebase. Refactoring costs increase whenever endpoints are added or parameters change, raising the risk of runtime errors due to a lack of type safety.

Spring Cloud OpenFeign provides an abstraction layer that declaratively defines HTTP request templates by combining Java interfaces with Spring MVC annotations. This article outlines the steps from introducing OpenFeign dependencies to interface design, endpoint integration, test execution verification, and handling configuration issues commonly encountered in production.

Enabling Dependencies and Features

To use OpenFeign, you must add the starter dependency to your build script and annotate the application to include it in the context scan targets.

Gradle Configuration (build.gradle) 

dependencies {
 implementation 'org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-starter-web'
 implementation 'org.springframework.cloud:spring-cloud-starter-openfeign'
 testImplementation 'org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-starter-test'
}

Enabling in the Bootstrap Class

Annotate the Spring application class or configuration class with @EnableFeignClients to instruct the generation of dynamic proxies at runtime.

package com.example.feign;

import org.springframework.boot.SpringApplication;
import org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.SpringBootApplication;
import org.springframework.cloud.openfeign.EnableFeignClients;

@EnableFeignClients
@SpringBootApplication
public class OpenFeignApplication {
 public static void main(String[] args) {
 SpringApplication.run(OpenFeignApplication.class, args);
 }
}

Implementing Mock Endpoints and Feign Clients

Construct a standard REST controller as the communication target for verification, along with its corresponding declarative client interface.

Controller Implementation 

package com.example.feign;

import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.GetMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RestController;

@RequestMapping("/test")
@RestController
public class TestController {

 @GetMapping
 public String test() {
 System.out.println("Hello, World!");
 return "Hello, World!";
 }
}

FeignClient Interface Definition 

package com.example.feign;

import org.springframework.cloud.openfeign.FeignClient;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.GetMapping;

@FeignClient(name = "test", url = "http://localhost:8080/test")
public interface TestClient {
 @GetMapping
 String test();
}
  • name attribute: The identifier for the client, which also functions as the service ID when integrating with service discovery.
  • url attribute: Specifies the base URL of the target. When an explicit URL is provided, it bypasses name resolution by the discovery client and issues HTTP requests directly.

Execution Verification via Integration Testing

Using the Spring Boot integration test environment, verify that the proxy-generated TestClient within the context can actually call the endpoint and receive the expected response.

package com.example.feign;

import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Autowired;
import org.springframework.boot.test.context.SpringBootTest;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

@SpringBootTest(webEnvironment = SpringBootTest.WebEnvironment.DEFINED_PORT)
class OpenFeignApplicationTests {

 @Autowired
 private TestClient testClient;

 @Test
 void contextLoads() {
 String result = testClient.test();
 assertThat(result).isEqualTo("Hello, World!");
 }
}

Troubleshooting

1. NoSuchBeanDefinitionException (Client Bean Not Found)

⚠️ If the package containing @EnableFeignClients differs from the package where the @FeignClient interface resides, it will be omitted from component scanning, causing an error during context initialization.

org.springframework.beans.factory.NoSuchBeanDefinitionException: No qualifying bean of type 'com.example.feign.TestClient' available

Solution: Explicitly specify the base scan package, such as @EnableFeignClients(basePackages = "com.example.feign").

2. Explicit Control of Connection and Read Timeouts

🛠️ Under default settings, threads may be blocked for extended periods during network latency or when the target service hangs. Define per-client timeout values in application.yml.

feign:
 client:
 config:
 default:
 connectTimeout: 5000
 readTimeout: 5000
 loggerLevel: full

Execution Verification Logs

Example console logs and port monitoring output when executing ./gradlew test in a local environment.

$ ./gradlew test

> Task :compileJava UP-TO-DATE
> Task :processResources UP-TO-DATE
> Task :classes UP-TO-DATE
> Task :compileTestJava UP-TO-DATE
> Task :processTestResources NO-SOURCE
> Task :testClasses UP-TO-DATE
> Task :test

2026-08-29T10:15:22.103+09:00 INFO 4120 --- [ main] c.e.feign.OpenFeignApplicationTests : Starting OpenFeignApplicationTests using Java 17.0.12
2026-08-29T10:15:23.450+09:00 INFO 4120 --- [ main] o.s.b.w.embedded.tomcat.TomcatWebServer : Tomcat started on port 8080 (http) with context path ''
Hello, World!
2026-08-29T10:15:24.112+09:00 INFO 4120 --- [ main] c.e.feign.OpenFeignApplicationTests : Started OpenFeignApplicationTests in 2.215 seconds

BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 3s
3 actionable tasks: 1 executed, 2 up-to-date

```text

$ curl -i http://localhost:8080/test
HTTP/1.1 200 
Content-Type: text/plain;charset=UTF-8
Content-Length: 13
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 01:15:30 GMT

Hello, World!

Key Takeaways

  • 💡 Spring Cloud OpenFeignを利用することで、低レイヤーのHTTPハンドリングをインターフェース定義に委譲でき、通信コードの記述量を削減できます。
  • 💡 @EnableFeignClients のスキャン範囲と @FeignClient のURL/名前解決設定を正確に管理することが、安定したクライアントプロキシ生成の基本要件です。
  • 💡 本番構成では、タイムアウト設定やロギングレベルをプロファイル単位で調整し、サービス障害時の連鎖遮断を考慮した設計を行う必要があります。
